prompt: Put the stages of the model lifecycle in order, starting from data.
Which decision in the lifecycle belongs to the modeller rather than the platform?

choices.text: Which algorithm to fit
choices.why: Right. The platform runs the fitting the same way every time.

choices.text: Where the trained model is stored, and under which version
choices.why: Registration is the platform's.

choices.text: How the model answers requests from the website
choices.why: Deployment is the platform's.

choices.text: How the tables land each night before features are built
choices.why: That is data engineering before any model exists.

prompt: Where do model projects fail most often, according to the lesson?

choices.text: In choosing the algorithm
choices.why: Algorithms are the part libraries already solved.

choices.text: A notebook model nobody rebuilds
choices.why: Right. The person who made it moves on, and the data they gathered by hand goes with them.

choices.text: In training, because it needs a graphics card
choices.why: Every model in this course trains on a processor in seconds.

choices.text: In evaluation, because scores are hard to compute
choices.why: They are one function call; agreeing which one matters is the hard part.

prompt: What does project.py's SHOP give every step?

choices.text: A copy of the database for each step
choices.why: It is a path, not a copy.

choices.text: A lock so two steps cannot read it at once
choices.why: Nothing in it locks anything.

choices.text: Its full path, from any directory
choices.why: Right. No more empty shop.db created by a run from the wrong place.

choices.text: The cutoff the step should use
choices.why: Cutoffs are arguments now, written in pipeline.sh.

prompt: Which problems of the earlier scripts does splitting into steps fix? Choose every one that applies.

choices.text: files found relative to wherever the program started
choices.why: Right. project.py names them in full.

choices.text: dates hidden inside the code
choices.why: Right. They are arguments now.

choices.text: nothing checking the rows
choices.why: Right. validate.py does.

choices.text: a model that ranks badly
choices.why: Steps change how a model is made, not how good it is.

prompt: build_dataset.py refuses 2026-01-31. What does it compare to decide?

choices.text: The cutoff with today's date on the computer
choices.why: It reads the data, so a late load is caught too.

choices.text: The number of members against 1,000
choices.why: That check is validate.py's.

choices.text: The cutoff against the newest model's training date
choices.why: It knows nothing about models.

choices.text: The cutoff plus 90 days with the last day of purchases
choices.why: Right. 1 May against 28 February.

prompt: How many members are in data/train.csv, as of 2025-08-31?
Why does it matter that a refused step exits with status 1 rather than printing a warning and carrying on?

choices.text: It is how a pipeline sees a failure
choices.why: Right. A pipeline knows a step failed only from its exit status, and with set -e the steps after it never run.

choices.text: Status 1 deletes the files the step wrote
choices.why: The step wrote nothing; the status itself deletes nothing.

choices.text: Because Python cannot print to a terminal from a pipeline
choices.why: It prints fine; a printed warning just stops nothing.

choices.text: Warnings are hidden by the orchestrator
choices.why: They may be logged; what stops the next task is the status.

prompt: Match each check in validate.py to what it would catch.
A contract check starts failing every night. What is the wrong first fix?

choices.text: Find out what changed in the data
choices.why: That is the right first step.

choices.text: Widen the range until the rows pass
choices.why: Right. It silences the one check that noticed.

choices.text: Ask the modeller whether the range still makes sense
choices.why: That is a reasonable second step, once the cause is known.

choices.text: Read the rows the check refused
choices.why: That is how the cause is found.

prompt: For how many members did validate.py report a negative recency in data/broken.csv?
What does data_sha256 in the training record let you say about two models?

choices.text: That they will score the same on any test
choices.why: Same data is not same code or same settings.

choices.text: Which version of features.py built them
choices.why: It names the data, not the code; lesson 7 adds the code.

choices.text: Same fingerprint, same training rows
choices.why: Right. Whatever the files were called.

choices.text: That they used the same scikit-learn
choices.why: That is another field of the record.

prompt: Why does the record keep the scikit-learn version?

choices.text: To bill the library's authors
choices.why: scikit-learn is free.

choices.text: Newer versions train better models
choices.why: Not necessarily, and that is not why it is recorded.

choices.text: joblib refuses to save without it
choices.why: joblib saves without being told.

choices.text: It only loads reliably in that version
choices.why: Right. Upgrading the library is then a decision with a record.

prompt: Why does evaluate.py load the model from disk instead of using the one train.py had in memory?

choices.text: It scores the file that would be deployed
choices.why: Right. Not an object that existed only while training ran.

choices.text: Loading from disk is faster
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: Python cannot pass a model between programs any other way
choices.why: The point is which artefact gets scored, not how.

choices.text: The model in memory had seen the test rows
choices.why: It had not; train.py never reads test.csv.

prompt: The pipeline's model scores 0.793 AUC and 190 in the top 300; lesson 4's scored 0.790 and 195. What should you conclude?

choices.text: The pipeline made the model better
choices.why: Three thousandths of AUC is noise here.

choices.text: Nothing: it is noise
choices.why: Right. Training on a different month moves scores this much; worth knowing before celebrating the next small change.

choices.text: The pipeline made the model worse
choices.why: Five members in three hundred is noise too.

choices.text: That one of the two has a leak
choices.why: A leak shows as a score too good, not a tiny difference.

prompt: What does set -e do in pipeline.sh?

choices.text: Makes every command print what it runs
choices.why: That is set -x.

choices.text: Runs the steps in parallel
choices.why: They run one after another.

choices.text: Stops the script at the first command that fails
choices.why: Right. A refused dataset never reaches train.py.

choices.text: Exports the environment to the Python steps
choices.why: Exporting is a different command.

prompt: What does an orchestrator such as Airflow add to pipeline.sh, and what does it leave unchanged?

choices.text: It replaces the four steps with one task
choices.why: Each step stays a task of its own.

choices.text: It rewrites the steps in its own language
choices.why: It runs the same programs.

choices.text: It makes the dataset step unnecessary
choices.why: Someone still has to build the examples.

choices.text: Retries, history and alerts; same steps
choices.why: Right. A file in and a file out is exactly the shape it expects.

prompt: What is training-serving skew?

choices.text: The same feature, computed two ways
choices.why: Right. The model gets numbers that mean something else.

choices.text: A model served faster than it was trained
choices.why: Speed has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: A test set from a later month than the training set
choices.why: That is the honest split, not a skew.

choices.text: Training on more members than are served
choices.why: Numbers of members are not the issue.

prompt: With the website's features, how many members' probabilities moved by more than 0.1?
Why did nothing raise an error when the website sent spend in reais?

choices.text: scikit-learn ignores columns it does not recognise
choices.why: It recognised them: the names were right.

choices.text: Valid numbers, right names
choices.why: Right. Only the meaning changed, and no type check sees meaning.

choices.text: The model had been trained on reais as well
choices.why: It learned cents; that is the skew.

choices.text: Because AUC only fell to 0.770
choices.why: A score falling raises no error either.

prompt: What is the defence the lesson recommends against skew?

choices.text: Asking every team to be more careful with units
choices.why: Everybody was careful; care is not a mechanism.

choices.text: Retraining the model on the website's features
choices.why: Then the batch scores would be skewed instead.

choices.text: One implementation of the features, used by training and serving
choices.why: Right. Lesson 6 turns it into a feature store.

choices.text: Rounding every feature to whole numbers
choices.why: Rounding does not convert reais into cents.

prompt: Why ask for the label defined in code rather than in a sentence?

choices.text: Sentences cannot be stored in Git
choices.why: They can; the problem is reimplementing them.

choices.text: Code runs faster than a sentence
choices.why: A sentence does not run at all.

choices.text: Modellers do not write sentences
choices.why: They do; the point is which one is authoritative.

choices.text: A sentence is two implementations waiting to differ
choices.why: Right. Is lapsed 90 days or three months? The code says.

prompt: Which of these should come with a model before a data engineer takes it on? Choose every one that applies.

choices.text: the label's maturity
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: the deciding score and its baseline
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: who uses the output, and how
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: the modeller's notebook, with its outputs
choices.why: The definitions belong in code that runs; a notebook's outputs are a record of one run.

prompt: The nightly training run starts producing a model whose said is 0.31 while the test's lapse share is 0.17. Which step should have stopped it?

choices.text: build_dataset.py or validate.py
choices.why: Right. A model saying 0.31 learned a lapse rate near that: look for unfinished labels.

choices.text: evaluate.py, which should refuse low AUC
choices.why: A calibration problem can come with a fine AUC.

choices.text: train.py, which should use more iterations
choices.why: More iterations fit the same wrong labels more closely.

choices.text: pipeline.sh, which should run less often
choices.why: How often it runs does not decide what it learns.

A model is a data product whose output is a guess about the ___.
